- Good: M20, M14, M11, M9, M16 (-39.1 to -39.6) — deactivation mechanisms

Key insight: M3 (2cat⇌cat2, substrate reacts with dimer) and M4 (X-mediated pathway) fit best — both have nonlinear catalyst dependence. Deactivation mechanisms (M9, M11, M14, M16, M20) also do well since high catalyst gives fast reaction that can plateau.

Aim achieved — significant discrimination now visible.

Next, I want to discriminate:
1. M3 vs. M4 — both show nonlinear catalyst behavior. M3 has reversible dimer (equilibrium); M4 has X catalyst that transforms catS→S+cat or catS→P+cat.
2. Deactivation mechanisms: M9 (cat→inactive), M11 (S+cat→inactive), M14 (catS→inactive), M16 (S+catS→inactive), M20 (both cat and catS deactivate)
3. Separate these from non-deactivation mechanisms.

A low-catalyst, high-substrate, long-time experiment would help:
- If deactivation is present (M9, M11, M14, M16, M20), reaction won't reach completion
- M3: with low [cat], dimer concentration ∝ [cat]² is very small → effectively linear catalyst dependence; distinguishes from M11/M9 etc.
- M4: X is from catalyst, so at low [cat], less X → slow reaction

Alternatively, an experiment with added product tests product inhibition (M12, M17) — but these are already looking unlikely.

Better: high substrate, moderate catalyst. This tests substrate inhibition (M11, M16) vs. substrate activation (M3, M4 should not show inhibition). M11 (S+cat→inactive) and M16 (S+catS→inactive) predict slower reaction with high S.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
Propose high substrate, moderate catalyst experiment to distinguish substrate-inhibited mechanisms (M11, M16) from catalyst dimer/non-linear mechanisms (M3, M4) and from other deactivation mechanisms (M9, M14, M20):

- M11, M16: higher [S] → faster deactivation → reaction stalls earlier at lower conversion
- M9, M14, M20: deactivation rate independent of [S], so higher [S] → more turnovers before death
- M3: higher [S] simply saturates the dimer; faster initial rate, full conversion
- M4: higher [S] → higher rate through catS; full conversion

Conditions: S = 3.0 (high), cat = 0.01 (moderate/low), P = 0.0.
Low catalyst ensures long observation window; high S stresses substrate-dependent mechanisms.
</hypothesis>
